content: This guide covers modules, reload behavior, creator workflow, and flow testing.

content.text: Use this as a template and feature reference.

content: Sections:
Header controls:
- SCRIPT: switch bundled, custom and module scripts, or upload JSON
- CREATOR: edit the active script or start a new one
- MODULES: your modules, subscriptions and Show in Script choices
- LIBRARY: browse, rate and subscribe to published modules
- OPTIONS: sound, header, print, reload, clear local data, reset, theme
- SUPPORT: send feedback, donate, GitHub (+ ADMIN PANEL for admins)
- SIGN IN / PROFILE: email, username, account ID, sign out
- On narrow screens these fold into the MENU button
Feedback:
- SUPPORT > FEEDBACK sends a bug report, feature request or general feedback
- MY FEEDBACK lists what you've sent, its status, and any reply
- A number on SUPPORT means an admin has replied
Phones and tablets:
- Tap a prompt, login or table QUERY line to bring up the keyboard
- Tap anywhere else to close it
Preview mode details:
- Header shows [PREVIEW MODE] + [RETURN TO CREATOR]
- Flow runs in the real terminal renderer
- Use it before publishing modules
Every shortcut the app listens for.
Shortcuts are ignored while text is being entered: in a terminal
prompt or login, and in any text field (script creator, library
search, report composer).
Shift + H .......... show / hide the top header bar
Shift + Space ...... skip the typing animation on the current screen
Ctrl + Shift + L ... bypass a login on the current screen; submits
the login's first credential, so it lands on
whatever that credential targets. Does nothing
on a screen without a login.
letters / numbers .. enter text
Backspace .......... delete the last character
Enter .............. submit the command
letters / numbers .. enter text
Enter .............. submit the username, then the password
Backspace .......... delete the last character
Escape ............. close the dialog
Enter .............. close the dialog (when it has no action buttons)
Up / Down .......... move within the focused list
Left / Right ....... switch between the folder list and the file list
Enter .............. open a folder's files, or activate a button
Home / End ......... jump to the first / last entry
Backspace / Esc .... return focus from the file list to the folder list
Up / Down .......... move the row cursor
Enter .............. open the selected row
1 - 9 .............. sort by that column (again to reverse)
/ .................. open the QUERY line (or click / tap it)
Esc ................ clear the query
Left / Right ....... previous / next page (PgUp / PgDn too)
Shift + click ...... alternate action on a link, toggle, or list,
where the script defines one
Press and hold ..... same as Shift + click, for touch screens
Tap a prompt ....... opens the phone keyboard (tap elsewhere to close)
Visibility modes:
- private: visible only to your account
- unlisted: available through direct link and hidden from library listings
- public: visible in the library and shareable
Modules panel:
- My Modules: load, view in library, copy link, Manage > Edit Details
- Subscribed Modules: load, view in library
- Show in Script checkboxes decide what appears in the SCRIPT dropdown;
your choices are saved to your account, so they follow you
Library:
- OPTIONS > Web View (the default) or Terminal View
- Search, sort, subscribe, and rate 1-5 (Remove rating takes it back)
- Public and unlisted modules have share links
Usernames and credits:
- Every account gets a random username. You're asked once to keep it
or choose your own, and can change it any time under PROFILE
- The Library shows modules as "By <username>"
- Credit co-authors under Edit Details by pasting their account ID
(they copy it from PROFILE > ACCOUNT ID). Anyone credited can
remove themselves
1) Open CREATOR from header.
2) Use NEW SCRIPT to start clean, or edit the active script.
3) Build screens from the left list; dialogs are in a dedicated list mode.
4) Add elements from the Add Element menu.
5) Use [CONFIG: ON/OFF] to show or hide script config fields.
6) Use [SCHEMA] to inspect connection flow across screens/dialogs.
7) PREVIEW in runtime, then APPLY TO APP.
8) Save/update as a module from the Modules panel.
Editor helpers:
- Data Table: [GRID] edits it like a spreadsheet, [TEXT] for pasting
pipe-separated rows (a | b | c >> screen-id)
- Class Names: chips. + ADD CLASS adds one, x removes it; a new color
or blend mode replaces the old one
- Images: a Background field so blend modes work on dark themes

content.text: Use Creator for quick iteration, flow debugging, and module publishing.

content: Top-level shape:
"config": { "name": "My Script", "author": "You" },
"screens": [ ... ],
"dialogs": [ ... ]
Config options:
name, author ........ shown in the header and the Library
theme ............... blue, amber, green, white, light, or custom
customTheme ......... colors when theme is "custom" (bgHex, fgHex, ...)
defaultTextSpeed .... ms per typed character, whole script
terminalType ........ "alien" wraps every screen in file-system chrome
alien.title ......... default title bar text for that chrome
script .............. id of an optional terminal script (see ADVANCED)
Screen shape:
"id": "unique-id",
"type": "screen" | "static" | "filesystem",
"content": [ ... ],
"onDone": { "target": "next-id", "delayMs": 1200 },
"defaultTextSpeed": 40,   (this screen only)
"title": "...",           (its label in a file-system list)
"headerTitle": "..."      (file-system title bar text)
screen = progressive render, static = immediate render
filesystem = three-region file browser (see FILE SYSTEM SCREENS)
All content appears at once. Useful for status boards and dense menus.
Element map (creator label -> JSON shape):
- Text Line -> "plain string"
- Text Block / Alert / Notice / Emphasis / System -> { "type": "text", "text": "..." }
- Link Button -> { "type": "link", "text": "...", "target": "screenId" | [targets] }
- Bitmap/Image -> { "type": "bitmap" | "image", "src": "..." }
- Data Table -> { "type": "table", "columns": [...], "rows": [...] }
- Prompt Input -> { "type": "prompt", "prompt": "...", "caseSensitive": true|false, "cursor": true|false, "commands": [...] }

- Login Prompt -> { "type": "login", "usernameCaseSensitive": true|false, "hideUsername": true|false, "passwordCaseSensitive": true|false, "hidePassword": true|false, "credentials": [...], "noMatchAction": {...} }
- Toggle -> { "type": "toggle", "states": [...] }
- List -> { "type": "list", "states": [...] }
- Dropdown -> { "type": "dropdown", "states": [...] }
- Report Composer -> { "type": "reportComposer", "titleTemplate": "...", "template": "..." }
- Report List -> { "type": "reportList", "composerId": "..." }
- Dialog Link (+ Dialog) -> link target entry { "type": "dialog", "target": "dialogId" } + dialogs[] row
- Href -> { "type": "href", ... } is the same as a link
- Mainframe Game -> { "type": "mainframegame" } (the APHELION arena game;
finishing it plays a terminal-shutdown ending, so it isn't demoed here)
On any element:
- className, align, speed, loop (see ADVANCED OPTIONS)
- scriptId: a name a terminal script uses to find and change it

content: The Report Composer wrote data and navigated using saveTarget.
Prompt #1 (case-sensitive, default):
- command must match exactly: ExactCase
Prompt #2 (case-insensitive + free input):
- command: LOGS (any letter case)
- any other non-empty input is logged to user logs

content.text: > PROMPT COMMAND ACTIONS (help / home / back / debug)

content: --- BEGIN USER LOGS ---
[NO USER LOG ENTRIES RECORDED]
--- END USER LOGS ---
Link target forms:
- "target": "screenId"
- "target": [ typed entries ]
Typed entry kinds:
- { type: "link", target: "screenId" }
- { type: "dialog", target: "dialogId" }
- { type: "href", target: "https://..." }
- { type: "action", action: "back"|"dialog"|"resetState", target?: "screenId" }
- add "shiftKey": true / false to pick an entry by Shift+click
Dialogs (dialogs[] entries with type "alert"):
- content: strings, text objects, bitmaps and prompts
- "showActions": true + "actions": [{ "label", "target"? }] adds buttons

content.text: > OPEN QUICK HELP DIALOG (SHIFT+CLICK TO GO HOME)
> ACTION: RESET SCRIPT STATE + GO HOME

content: Useful optional properties:
- speed (per-element typing speed)
- defaultTextSpeed (screen or config level)
- loop (repeat object elements N times)
- onDone (auto-advance with optional delayMs)
- allowFreeInput + inputAction + caseSensitive on prompts
- fillWidth / scale / animated for bitmap/image
- align: "left" | "center" | "right" | "justify" (any element)
Terminal scripts (bundled scripts only):
- config.script names a TypeScript module in src/scripts/terminal/
- it can react to screens, prompts, links and toggles, and change any
element that has a "scriptId" (INCR-SS-ARK uses this)
Slow line:
Fast line:
Loop separator:
A screen with "type": "filesystem" renders a three-region file
browser inside its own chrome (a title bar over a framed viewport).
It is one self-contained view: selecting things updates it in place
and never changes screens.
- the screen's link elements are the FOLDERS (left column)
- a folder's target screen supplies the FILE list (top right):
- that target's own link elements are the files, or
- if the target has no links, the target itself is one file
- the selected file's target supplies the CONTENT (bottom right)
- headerTitle (on the file system screen): title bar text
- title (on a content screen): the name shown in the file list
- info file: if a folder's target has text as well as links, that
text becomes a file named after the folder, listed first
- buttons: a folder or file whose target is an ARRAY navigates or
runs an action instead of opening content, e.g.
"target": [ { "type": "action", "action": "back" } ]
- back links: a link pointing back at the file system screen itself
is hidden, so a converted screen's "< BACK" link is not listed
- content: file bodies render the same elements a normal screen
does, including class names, markdown, images, and prompts
Setting config.terminalType to "alien" wraps every screen in the
same chrome, so classic screens sit inside the framed viewport too.
It is not required: a "filesystem" screen brings its own chrome.

A table element prints a box-drawn database grid, one line at a time.
Once printed it becomes a live record browser:
- UP/DOWN moves the cursor, ENTER opens the row's target
- 1-9 (or clicking a heading) sorts by that column; again to reverse
- / opens the QUERY line to filter rows, ESC clears it
- LEFT/RIGHT or PGUP/PGDN pages through long tables
A read-only status table with the double border and no footer:
Keyed rows, colored cells, a default sort, and a row that runs an action
(the medical stores row opens a dialog):
An empty table shows its emptyText:
JSON shape:
{ "type": "table", "title": "...", "columns": ["ID", { "label": "LOAD", "align": "right" }],
"rows": [["001", "MORLEY"], { "cells": [...], "target": "screenId", "className": "alert" }],
"sortable": true, "filter": true, "pageSize": 8, "border": "single | double | ascii | none" }
Rows can also be objects keyed by column key, a cell can be { "text", "className" },
and a row target can be any link target (screen id or [targets] array).
A bitmap (or image) element draws a picture that resolves from big pixels to full detail.
Options:
- src / alt, scale (1 = natural size), fillWidth, animated (GIFs)
- align: "left" | "center" | "right"
- className: ONE blend mode, plus footer and/or script-hidden (separate with spaces)
- background: a color plate behind the image (fg, bg, alert, notice, emphasis, system, or any CSS color)

content.text: [FILL WIDTH]  "fillWidth": true  (stretches to the screen width)

content: Blend modes mix the image with what is behind it. Some look great on the dark
terminal; the darkening ones need a background color to show up.

content.text: > BLEND MODES FOR THE DARK TERMINAL
IMAGES: BLEND MODES FOR THE DARK TERMINAL

content: These blend modes work straight on the terminal background.

content.text: [monochrome]  grayscale, tinted by the background (same as luminosity)
[lighten]  black areas take the background color

content: On their own these modes leave the image almost black:
Give the image a "background" and they mix with that color instead:
hue and color keep the BACKGROUND's brightness, so on a flat plate the
picture flattens into a wash of its own colors:
"background" takes a theme color (fg, bg, alert, notice, emphasis, system)
or any CSS color such as "#ffffff" or "rgb(255 180 0)".
monochrome + a background tints the picture in that color:

content.text: [COMBINED]  className: "monochrome footer", background: emphasis, align: center

content: Dialogs have a bright background, so darkening modes work there without one:

content.text: > OPEN AN IMAGE IN A DIALOG

content: - Data tables: box-drawn record browsers you can sort, search and page
- Images: blend modes that work, background plates, alignment, footer
- Class names combine: "alert small center"
- File-system screens: links and table rows open files in place
- LANTERN-7: an original showcase scenario for the file-system screen
- Phones and tablets: tap a prompt, login or QUERY line to type
- A modern Web View (now the default) alongside Terminal View
- Usernames: pick one on first sign-in, change it under PROFILE
- Co-authors: credit other creators by their account ID
- Star ratings, and you can remove your rating
- Show in Script choices are saved to your account
- SUPPORT > FEEDBACK: bug reports, feature requests, general feedback
- MY FEEDBACK shows each message's status and any reply
- Security hardening, faster loading, updated dependencies
Text lines support a small set of markdown:
# A heading line
**bold**, *italic*, __underline__ and ~~strikethrough~~
[an external link](https://example.com)
- a bullet point
> a quoted line
\> a line that starts with a literal > (escaped)
\# A heading line
\*\*bold\*\*, \*italic\*, \_\_underline\_\_ and \~\~strikethrough\~\~
\[an external link\](https://example.com)
\- a bullet point
\> a quoted line
(a backslash before a markdown character shows it as-is)
A state can do more than change the text. Click each one:

content.text: [COLORED STATES]  each state has its own className
[OPENS A DIALOG]  "dialog": switching to this state shows a dialog
[GUARDED]  "dialog" + "requireShift": click shows the dialog, Shift+click switches
[NAVIGATES]  "target": switching to this state opens a screen

content: Tables work inside file-system files too. Click the table, then use the keys.
Before shipping your script/module:
- Verify all screen IDs are unique
- Verify all link/dialog/action targets resolve
- Preview full flow, including prompts and dialogs
- Confirm Scripts dropdown visibility choices in Modules panel
- Validate module links from Modules and Library views
- Export JSON backup when stable
- Set your username (PROFILE) and credit co-authors (Edit Details)
- Check your module's Library page in Web View and Terminal View
